introduction_markdown: CAMEROON GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION BOARD, General Certificate of Education Examination. 0585 RELIGIOUS STUDIES 1, JUNE 2019, ORDINARY LEVEL. Multiple choice question paper, one and a half hours. Mobile phones are NOT allowed in the examination room. Instructions to candidates: use a soft HB pencil throughout the examination; do not open the booklet until told to do so; check that the booklet is headed Ordinary Level - 0585 Religious Studies 1. Answer all 50 questions in this examination. Each question has FOUR suggested answers: A, B, C and D. Decide which answer is appropriate, find the number of the question on the answer sheet and draw a horizontal line across the letter to join the square brackets for the answer you have chosen. Mark only one answer for each question: if you mark more than one answer you will score a zero for that question; if you change your mind, erase the first mark carefully, then mark your new answer. Avoid spending too much time on any one question; you can come back to it later. Do all rough work in the booklet using the blank spaces. At the end of the examination the invigilator collects the answer sheet first and then the question booklet. Printed heading of the questions: PERSONAL AND SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS AND PROBLEMS.

questions.enonce_markdown: The selfless giving of oneself even to the point of death is
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Agape** is the unconditional, self-giving love that seeks the good of the other even at great cost, including death. Conjugal love is the love between spouses, erotic love is passionate attraction, and phila (philia) is the love between friends.

**Answer: D.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - friendship and love

questions.enonce_markdown: An extravagant and short-lived passion is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Infatuation** is an intense, exaggerated attraction that does not last because it rests on appearance or on feelings of the moment. Eros is romantic or sexual love in general, philia is lasting friendship, and emotions is too general a word.

**Answer: C.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - friendship and love

questions.enonce_markdown:
Marriage is purposefully meant for procreation and---?

*Options as printed:* A) unity.   B) love.   C) companionship.   D) fidelity
questions.corrige_markdown:
Marriage is meant for procreation and for companionship, that is, mutual help and support between husband and wife. Unity, love and fidelity are qualities of a good marriage, but they are not usually given as its two purposes in the programme.

**Intended answer: C (companionship).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - marriage and family

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which word best qualifies the union between a man and a woman?

*Options as printed:* A) Contract   B) Marriage   C) Agreement   D) Union
questions.corrige_markdown:
The lasting, publicly recognised union of a man and a woman is called **marriage**. A contract or an agreement is a legal or business arrangement, and union is the word already used in the question.

**Intended answer: B (Marriage).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - marriage and family

questions.enonce_markdown: In our days and for fear to marry the wrong partner, ------marriage is popular.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Trial** marriage (living together before marrying, to test compatibility) is the form that people choose out of fear of marrying the wrong partner. Same-sex and civil marriage are not motivated by this fear, and mixed marriage is a union between people of different backgrounds.

**Answer: C.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - marriage and family

questions.enonce_markdown:
Whenever a woman puts to birth, the child is either a boy or a girl. This fact describes:

*Options as printed:* A) human sexuality.   B) the sex organ.   C) male or female.   D) sexual morality.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The fact that a newborn is either a boy or a girl describes the distinction **male or female**. Human sexuality is the wider reality of being sexual persons, the sex organ is only a body part, and sexual morality concerns right conduct.

**Intended answer: C (male or female).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sexuality and chastity

questions.enonce_markdown:
Why is prostitution bad?

*Options as printed:* A) Some customers don't pay.   B) It can lead to unwanted pregnancy.   C) The reason is only money.   D) It is sinful.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Prostitution is judged wrong mainly on moral and religious grounds, because it treats the person as an object of sale and goes against chastity. Both B and D name a consequence or a ground of the wrong, so this item is not a reliable single-answer question.

**Intended answer: D (It is sinful).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sexuality and chastity

questions.enonce_markdown:
It is a solution to indiscriminate sex.

*Options as printed:* A) Prostitution.   B) Rape.   C) Polygyny.   D) Adultery.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The printed options all describe wrong or disputed practices, and the question does not say from whose point of view something is a solution. The intended answer is probably polygyny, which some societies present as a remedy for indiscriminate sex, but this is a matter of local convention.

**Intended answer: C (Polygyny).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sexuality and chastity

questions.enonce_markdown: Sexual advances as a condition for love ---- relationship.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Demanding sexual favours as a condition for love turns the relationship into an exchange and a pressure, so it **kills love**. Real love is free and respectful, so the other three options, which say it improves love, are wrong.

**Answer: A.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - friendship and love

questions.enonce_markdown: When a child lacks proper upbringing, he is likely to be all BUT ONE of the following to the family and society at large:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A child without proper upbringing is likely to become a failure, a threat and a handicap (a burden) to the family and society. **A hawker** is simply a street seller, a trade and not a result of poor upbringing, so it is the odd one out.

**Answer: D.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - marriage and family

questions.enonce_markdown: If "A" delays the payment of his brother's hospital bill because his arrears have not come and "B" pays it in anger, and boasts about it until there is disunity in the family: What can we say is the main cause of the disunity?
questions.corrige_markdown:
B paid the bill in anger and kept boasting about it. The root of the quarrel is therefore **pride** (boasting), not poverty, the bill or the illness, which are only the occasions.

**Answer: A.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - marriage and family

questions.enonce_markdown:
A street child could be described as a

*Options as printed:* A) perigrinus.   B) vagus.   C) incola.   D) vagabond.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A street child is commonly described as a vagabond (a homeless wanderer). The Latin words in the options are unfamiliar and ambiguous, so the item is not reliable for automatic marking.

**Intended answer: D (vagabond).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - marriage and family

questions.enonce_markdown: Someone bringing up a family alone is
questions.corrige_markdown:
The question says "someone", with no gender, so the right term is **a single parent**, which covers a mother or a father. "A single mother" is too narrow, and being unmarried or responsible does not describe the situation.

**Answer: C.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - marriage and family

questions.enonce_markdown: Birth control means all but ONE of the following:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Birth control means choosing when to have a child and how many children to have, and some traditions add having them only in marriage. Choosing the **sex** of the child is not birth control, so B is the exception.

**Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sanctity of life and bioethics

choix.texte: Getting a child when it is most convenient.
Getting a child of the required sex.
Getting the required number of children.
Getting a child only in wedlock.

questions.enonce_markdown: Birth control for the purpose of limiting or spacing out the number children in a family is known as
questions.corrige_markdown:
Limiting or spacing the number of children in a family is called **family planning**. The other terms are not the standard name for it.

**Answer: C.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sanctity of life and bioethics

questions.enonce_markdown:
A doctor is a worker just as a farmer is a worker. For what reason are they working?

*Options as printed:* A) To save life   B) To make life meaningful   C) To sustain   D) To earn money
questions.corrige_markdown:
The question does not say which reason is meant, and the options are not clearly separated: a doctor and a farmer both work to earn a living, to sustain life and to give meaning to life. The intended answer is probably B, but the item is too open for automatic marking.

**Intended answer: B (To make life meaningful).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - work and leisure

questions.enonce_markdown: All BUT ONE of these are abuses of leisure.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Idleness, loitering and wasting money are abuses of leisure. A **change of activity** is a healthy use of free time (rest, recreation), so it is the exception.

**Answer: C.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - work and leisure

questions.enonce_markdown: While work is important, we need time off duty known as
questions.corrige_markdown:
Free time away from work, used for rest and recreation, is called **leisure**. Break, rest and public holiday describe parts or kinds of time off, but leisure is the general term.

**Answer: D.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - work and leisure

questions.enonce_markdown: A trade union or workers syndicate is
questions.corrige_markdown:
A trade union is a **free (voluntary) association of workers** that defends their rights and interests. Workers cannot be forced to join, so the compulsory and necessary options are wrong.

**Answer: A.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - work and leisure

questions.enonce_markdown: A research activity that creates a copy of some biological entity is better known as
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Cloning** is the production of a genetic copy of a living being. An organ transplant moves an organ from one body to another, and mutilation is the damaging of the body.

**Answer: C.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sanctity of life and bioethics

questions.enonce_markdown: An abortion done for medical reasons is
questions.corrige_markdown:
An abortion carried out for a medical reason, such as to save the mother's life, is a **therapeutic abortion**. A natural abortion is a miscarriage, and induced and direct abortion describe the method, not the medical purpose.

**Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sanctity of life and bioethics

questions.enonce_markdown:
It violates human life and is done by the person on his/her authority.

*Options as printed:* A) Abortion   B) Murder   C) Euthanasia   D) Suicide
questions.corrige_markdown:
The wording is unclear: suicide is a person's act on his or her own life, but murder, abortion and euthanasia also violate life. The intended answer is probably suicide, which is a personal act, but the item is too ambiguous for automatic marking.

**Intended answer: D (Suicide).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sanctity of life and bioethics

questions.enonce_markdown: Drug abuse is when
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Drug abuse** is the wrong use of a drug, that is, outside medical need or in the wrong quantity or way. Side effects, a herbalist's origin or long use do not by themselves make a use wrong.

**Answer: D.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - drugs and substance abuse

choix.texte: drugs with negative side effects are used.
drugs consumed are produced by a herbalist.
drugs are taken continuously for long.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Drug addiction is when a person

*Options as printed:* A) takes a particular drug for a long period.   B) depends on drugs for happiness.   C) cannot survive without the drug.   D) is unable to resist the consumption of a particular drug.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Addiction is a dependence in which the person cannot stop taking the drug. Options B, C and D can each be defended as a description of addiction, with D the best fit (loss of control), so the item is not reliable for automatic marking.

**Intended answer: D (is unable to resist the consumption of a particular drug).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - drugs and substance abuse

questions.enonce_markdown:
A disciplinary session is organized to judge Pa Ngwa, a class one school teacher who mercilessly beat his pupil. What conscience does Pa Ngwa have?

*Options as printed:* A) A lax conscience.   B) A wrong conscience.   C) A poorly formed conscience   D) An erroneous conscience.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Pa Ngwa's conscience could be called poorly formed, erroneous or wrong, since he mistakenly judges that harsh beating is acceptable. The terms overlap, so the item is not reliable for automatic marking.

**Intended answer: C (A poorly formed conscience).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - conscience and moral choice

questions.enonce_markdown: The decision to lock up the thief was based on the report presented by the victim of the theft. What kind of judgment was that?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The decision rests on a report of what happened, the facts reported by the victim, so it is a **judgment of fact**. Judgments of value or moral judgments say whether something is good or bad.

**Answer: A.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - conscience and moral choice

questions.enonce_markdown: Most people do evil, yet they do not bother. What is the possible reason for this poor attitude?
questions.corrige_markdown:
People who do evil without feeling concerned lack the inner voice that warns them, which is a **poorly formed conscience**. Conduct and habits are the results of conscience, and well-formed conduct cannot explain doing evil.

**Answer: C.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - conscience and moral choice

questions.enonce_markdown:
"CONAC" has not succeeded to stamp out corruption from Cameroon. What could be the reason for this failure?

*Options as printed:* A) It is corrupt itself   B) It does not punish criminals   C) The country is very corrupt   D) The members are very few
questions.corrige_markdown:
The question asks for an opinion on a particular institution, and several options can be argued (the institution's own weakness, lack of sanctions, widespread corruption). It is left open for self-assessment instead of being marked automatically.

**Intended answer: C (The country is very corrupt).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - corruption and embezzlement

questions.enonce_markdown:
Criminals should be punished with:

*Options as printed:* A) hatred,   B) revenge.   C) love.   D) kindness.
questions.corrige_markdown:
According to the Christian teaching that the programme follows, punishment should aim at correction and be guided by justice and love, not hatred or revenge. The answer depends on a moral position (and on whether love or kindness is meant), so the item is left open.

**Intended answer: C (love).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - justice and human rights

questions.enonce_markdown: Zechariah is a student who pays attention in watching movies, but seldom concentrates on his academics: What type of conscience does he have?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **lax conscience** treats serious matters lightly and gives importance to trivial things. Zechariah neglects his studies for films, so his conscience is lax. A perplexed conscience is torn between two evils, a doubtful one is unsure, and a certain one is firmly convinced.

**Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - conscience and moral choice

questions.enonce_markdown: Which tree is environmentally friendly with respect to the water table?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The **raffia palm** grows in wet, marshy places and does not drain the water table. The eucalyptus is known to draw large amounts of groundwater and dry the soil, so it is not water-friendly.

**Answer: C.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - environmental ethics

questions.enonce_markdown: The throwing of groundnuts and banana peelings anywhere in town goes against:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Littering goes against **environmental ethics**, the duty to keep our surroundings clean. Loyal ethics is not a recognised term.

**Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - environmental ethics

questions.enonce_markdown: The judiciary is meant to ensure
questions.corrige_markdown:
The judiciary, the courts, exists mainly to make sure that **justice** is done by applying the law and settling disputes. Equity, peace and order are results or aspects of justice.

**Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - justice and human rights

questions.enonce_markdown: When the terms of a contract are respected, how do we call that?
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Commutative justice** is justice in exchanges between individuals, such as keeping the terms of a contract. Legal justice is the citizen's duty to the community, social justice concerns the fair share of goods in society, and contributive justice concerns what each member gives to the group.

**Answer: D.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - justice and human rights

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the relation between justice and peace?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Where everyone is treated fairly, conflicts are fewer, so **justice brings peace**. They are related but not the same, and peace does not by itself produce justice.

**Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - justice and human rights

choix.texte: Justice has nothing to do with peace.
Peace is the same as justice..

questions.enonce_markdown: HIV/AIDS may NOT be gotten from:
questions.corrige_markdown:
HIV passes through unprotected sex, infected blood and unsterilised sharp instruments. Excessive drinking is not a way in which the virus is passed, although it may lead to careless behaviour, so **B** is the answer.

**Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - hiv and aids

questions.enonce_markdown: All EXCEPT ONE of these transmits HIV
questions.corrige_markdown:
Blood and sexual fluids transmit HIV. **Water** does not, because the virus cannot live in it. Saliva carries so little virus that it is not a real route, but water is the clear exception here.

**Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - hiv and aids

questions.enonce_markdown: Tribalism is a form of
questions.corrige_markdown:
Tribalism is giving unfair preference to people of one's own tribe, so it is a form of **favouritism**. Nepotism is favouritism toward relatives, and racism concerns race.

**Answer: C.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - justice and human rights

questions.enonce_markdown: A child who moves in the street selling groundnuts is undergoing
questions.corrige_markdown:
A young child sent to sell in the street is deprived of rest, school and safety, which is a form of **child abuse** (exploitation). It is not training or upbringing, and delinquency means the child's own wrongdoing.

**Answer: C.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - justice and human rights

questions.enonce_markdown: A general term for the crime of falsifying documents is
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Forgery** is the crime of making or altering documents in order to deceive. Counterfeiting is used for money and goods, and fraud is a wider term for cheating.

**Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - corruption and embezzlement

questions.enonce_markdown:
The illicit exposure of people's naked pictures on the internet without their consent is known as:

*Options as printed:* A) cybernetics.   B) Cyber sex.   C) Cyber crime.   D) Cyber-bullying.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Several options can be defended (cyber crime as a general class, cyber-bullying as the harm done to the victim), and the exact term is a matter of textbook convention, so the item is left open.

**Intended answer: C (Cyber crime).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - cyber ethics

questions.enonce_markdown: Fraudulent activity using the internet is known as
questions.corrige_markdown:
Cheating people on the internet to get their money or data is **scamming**. Cyber terrorism is an attack with political aims, and cybernetics is the study of control systems.

**Answer: A.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - cyber ethics

questions.enonce_markdown: ____is the illicit access to a website or network.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Hacking** is gaining access to a website or network without permission. Scamming is cheating, networking is the lawful connection of people or computers, and grafting is joining plant tissues.

**Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - cyber ethics

questions.enonce_markdown: The rules governing the correct and kind way of behaving on the net is
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Netiquette** (net etiquette) is the usual name for the rules of polite and correct behaviour on the internet.

**Answer: D.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - cyber ethics

questions.enonce_markdown: A Christian who goes to Church but still visits diviners is practicing
questions.corrige_markdown:
Following two sets of practices that contradict each other, going to church and consulting diviners, is called **double standards**. Idolatry is worship of idols, witchcraft is use of occult power to harm, and divination is the diviner's own practice.

**Answer: D.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - african traditional religion

questions.enonce_markdown: As Pa Arrey was going, a rat crossed from the right to the left, he nodded his head saying to himself: "that journey will be good". What does he believe in?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Believing that a chance event, such as an animal crossing the road, foretells good or bad luck is **superstition**. Divination uses a specialist and rituals, while witchcraft and sorcery involve harmful power.

**Answer: A.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - african traditional religion

questions.enonce_markdown: The use of the forces of nature for evil motives is commonly known as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Using the hidden forces of nature to harm others is commonly called **witchcraft**. Superstition is a belief in omens, and idolatry is worship of images.

**Answer: C.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - african traditional religion

questions.enonce_markdown:
Cults are like sects in that

*Options as printed:* A) They practice secrecy.   B) They are deviations from the original doctrines.   C) They have developed their own doctrines.   D) They have given a new interpretation to the older religious idea.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Both sects and cults depart from an older religion, but the options B, C and D can each be defended, so the item depends on a textbook's wording and is left open.

**Intended answer: B (They are deviations from the original doctrines).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sects and cults

questions.enonce_markdown:
A new Religious movement is recognized by the fact that it is

*Options as printed:* A) A break away group.   B) A separatist group.   C) An independent combination of many doctrines.   D) A mainstream Church.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A new religious movement is usually a new group that combines several teachings. A and B describe sects rather than new movements, and the option wording is loose, so the item is left open.

**Intended answer: C (An independent combination of many doctrines).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sects and cults

questions.enonce_markdown:
One main reason why sects continue to succeed is that

*Options as printed:* A) they preach the true message   B) they organize free Bible classes.   C) they make much use of the media.   D) they are "born again" Christians
questions.corrige_markdown:
Several reasons can be given for the success of sects (use of the media, promises of healing and prosperity, close community life), and the options are not equally defensible, so the item is left open.

**Intended answer: C (they make much use of the media).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sects and cults
